primitives.name: Weighted Conformal Prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model **Weighted split conformal**: compute nonconformity scores on the calibration fold; form the weighted empirical distribution Σ_i p̃_i δ_{V_i} + p̃_{n+1} δ_∞ where p̃_i ∝ w(X_i) (normalized INCLUDING the test point's weight); interval = weighted (1-α)-quantile.

The core insight of [1645] is that standard conformal prediction fails under covariate shift because it assumes identical marginal distributions between training and test sets. This leads to invalid coverage guarantees. The solution lies in reweighting calibration scores using the likelihood ratio w(x) = dP̃_X/dP_X, which adjusts for differences in input distributions while preserving the conditional outcome law P_{Y|X}. The key theoretical machinery is weighted exchangeability, which generalizes classical exchangeability to accommodate non-uniform sampling. From this, the weighted quantile lemma follows, ensuring that the resulting prediction intervals maintain finite-sample coverage. In practice, this requires estimating weights from data—typically via logistic regression distinguishing calibration from test samples—and applying them in a modified split conformal procedure. The method is validated on the airfoil dataset, showing improved coverage from 82.2% to 90.8% under simulated shift. For GSE, this translates directly into robust forecasting under regime changes such as playoff games or QB injuries, where feature distributions differ but outcomes remain governed by similar dynamics.
